candidates.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
candidates.finding: OpenAI publicly describes restricting frontier training runs to offline/cached web resources, layered sandbox and microVM isolation, network egress boundaries, monitoring, and adversarial tests for prohibited external access and cross-agent communication. The article distinguishes internal frontier research settings from deployed customer models and reports an October 1 resumption after remediation. These are OpenAI's reported practices, not an audited public implementation or permission to reuse infrastructure.
candidates.hilo_adaptation: Propose a non-ranking, simulated-only containment checklist for any future authorized HILO research-worker sandbox: log permitted network destinations and message channels; require denied-egress and isolation regression tests with synthetic fixtures; record when the monitor was active; halt/escalate on unexpected access. Maintain max_model_requests=0 and current no-post/no-deploy/no-capture gates. This does not prove HILO isolation, authorize penetration testing or security certification, or create real robot hours.

reviewed_not_admitted.reason: The challenge's long-horizon simulated household-task evaluation is already separately attributed in the HILO reference ledger. Its October 16 submission deadline has passed, and the reviewed page does not justify duplicating a new source card or claiming field hours.
